observed_evidence: U.S. Central Command commander Admiral Brad Cooper said oil and LNG shipments through the Strait of Hormuz during the prior two weeks reached their highest level in six months. He said primary transit lanes were clear of mines and attributed improvement to naval protection and mine-clearance operations. This is an official military assessment; no unverified daily throughput number is inserted.
semantic_interpretation: Material partial de-escalation versus the prior snapshot's extremely low vessel counts. It reduces the immediate probability of a complete Hormuz energy-flow interruption and should temper oil/LNG/freight tail-risk, but it is not treated as normalization because regional hostilities, Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure, Red Sea risk and Saudi bypass-pipeline damage remain unresolved.
